title: Node.js Mastery
subtitle: Complete Guide from Beginner to Advanced
author: Systems Programming Experts

chapters.title: Introduction to Node.js
chapters.description: Learn the fundamentals of Node.js, its architecture, features, and how it differs from browser-based JavaScript. Understand event-driven programming and non-blocking I/O.

pages.title: What is Node.js?
pages.content: Node.js is a runtime environment that allows you to run JavaScript on the server side. It is built on Chrome's V8 engine and is widely used for building scalable backend applications.
pages.exampleCode:
// Simple Node.js program
console.log('Hello Node.js');
keyPoints: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser

quiz.question: What is Node.js?
quiz.explanation: Node.js is a runtime environment for executing JavaScript.

pages.title: Features of Node.js
pages.content: Node.js offers several powerful features such as asynchronous processing, event-driven architecture, and high performance.

quiz.question: Which feature makes Node.js fast?
quiz.explanation: Node.js uses event-driven architecture for high performance.

pages.title: Node.js vs Browser JavaScript
pages.content: JavaScript in the browser is used for frontend development, while Node.js allows JavaScript to run on the server side for backend development.
keyPoints: Node.js has access to file system

quiz.question: Where does Node.js run?
quiz.explanation: Node.js runs on the server side.

pages.title: Event-driven Architecture
pages.content: Node.js uses an event-driven architecture where operations are executed based on events. This allows handling multiple requests efficiently.

quiz.question: What triggers actions in Node.js event-driven model?
quiz.explanation: Events trigger actions in event-driven architecture.

pages.title: Non-blocking I/O
pages.content: Non-blocking I/O allows Node.js to handle multiple operations without waiting for one task to complete before starting another.

quiz.question: What is non-blocking I/O?
quiz.explanation: Non-blocking I/O allows asynchronous execution of tasks.

chapters.title: Setup & Environment
chapters.description: Learn how to install Node.js, explore the REPL, use npm, create your first application, and understand the package.json configuration.

pages.title: Installing Node.js
pages.content: Node.js can be installed from the official website or using package managers. After installation, you can verify it using version commands.
pages.exampleCode:
# Check Node.js version
node -v

# Check npm version
npm -v

quiz.question: Which command checks Node.js version?
quiz.explanation: node -v displays the installed Node.js version.

pages.title: Node REPL
pages.content: REPL stands for Read-Eval-Print Loop. It allows you to execute JavaScript code directly in the terminal without creating a file.
pages.exampleCode:
# Start REPL
node

> 2 + 2
4

quiz.question: What does REPL stand for?
quiz.explanation: REPL stands for Read-Eval-Print Loop.

pages.title: npm (Node Package Manager)
pages.content: npm is used to install, manage, and share packages (libraries) in Node.js applications.
pages.exampleCode:
# Install package
npm install express

# Install globally
npm install -g nodemon

quiz.question: What is npm used for?
quiz.explanation: npm is used to manage Node.js packages.

pages.title: Creating First App
pages.content: You can create a simple Node.js application by writing JavaScript code in a file and running it using Node.

quiz.question: How do you run a Node.js file?
quiz.explanation: node app.js runs the application.

pages.title: package.json
pages.content: package.json is a configuration file that stores project metadata, dependencies, and scripts. It is essential for managing Node.js projects.

quiz.question: What is package.json used for?
quiz.explanation: package.json stores project configuration and dependencies.

chapters.title: Core Modules
chapters.description: Learn about built-in Node.js core modules such as File System, HTTP, Path, OS, and Events. These modules help in building server-side applications without external libraries.

pages.title: File System (fs) Module
pages.content: The fs module is used to interact with the file system. It allows reading, writing, updating, and deleting files.

quiz.question: Which module is used for file handling?
quiz.explanation: The fs module is used for file operations.

pages.title: HTTP Module
pages.content: The http module is used to create web servers and handle HTTP requests and responses.

quiz.question: Which module is used to create a server?
quiz.explanation: The http module is used to create servers.

pages.title: Path Module
pages.content: The path module helps handle and transform file paths. It ensures compatibility across different operating systems.

quiz.question: What does the path module do?
quiz.explanation: The path module is used for handling file paths.

pages.title: OS Module
pages.content: The os module provides information about the operating system such as CPU, memory, and platform details.

quiz.question: Which module provides system information?
quiz.explanation: The os module provides system-related information.

pages.title: Events Module
pages.content: The events module allows handling custom events using EventEmitter. It is a core part of Node.js event-driven architecture.

quiz.question: Which class is used for events?
quiz.explanation: EventEmitter is used to handle events.

chapters.title: Asynchronous Programming
chapters.description: Learn how Node.js handles asynchronous operations using callbacks, promises, and async/await. Understand the event loop and error handling mechanisms.

pages.title: Callbacks
pages.content: Callbacks are functions passed as arguments to other functions and executed after an operation completes. They are the basic way to handle asynchronous operations in Node.js.

quiz.question: What is a callback?
quiz.explanation: A callback is a function passed as an argument to another function.

pages.title: Promises
pages.content: Promises provide a cleaner way to handle asynchronous operations. They represent a value that may be available now, later, or never.

quiz.question: What does a promise represent?
quiz.explanation: A promise represents a value that will be available in the future.

pages.title: Async/Await
pages.content: Async/Await is a modern way to handle asynchronous code. It makes asynchronous code look like synchronous code, improving readability.

quiz.question: What does await do?
quiz.explanation: await pauses execution until the promise resolves.

pages.title: Event Loop
pages.content: The event loop is the core of Node.js that handles asynchronous operations. It processes callbacks and ensures non-blocking execution.

quiz.question: What is the role of event loop?
quiz.explanation: Event loop manages asynchronous execution.

pages.title: Error Handling
pages.content: Error handling in Node.js ensures that applications do not crash unexpectedly. It can be handled using try/catch for async/await or .catch() for promises.

quiz.question: Which is used for error handling in async/await?
quiz.explanation: try/catch is used for handling errors in async/await.

chapters.title: Express.js Framework
chapters.description: Learn how to build web applications using Express.js. This module covers routing, middleware, REST APIs, and handling HTTP requests and responses.

pages.title: Introduction to Express.js
pages.content: Express.js is a lightweight web framework for Node.js that simplifies building web servers and APIs.

quiz.question: What is Express.js?
quiz.explanation: Express.js is a web framework for Node.js.

pages.title: Routing
pages.content: Routing defines how an application responds to client requests for specific endpoints and HTTP methods.

quiz.question: What is routing in Express?
quiz.explanation: Routing handles how requests are processed in Express.

pages.title: Middleware
pages.content: Middleware functions are functions that execute during the request-response cycle. They can modify requests, responses, or end the request.

quiz.question: What does next() do in middleware?
quiz.explanation: next() passes control to the next middleware function.

pages.title: REST APIs
pages.content: REST APIs allow communication between client and server using HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.

quiz.question: Which method is used to fetch data?
quiz.explanation: GET is used to retrieve data from server.

pages.title: Request & Response
pages.content: The request object contains client data, while the response object is used to send data back to the client.

quiz.question: What does res.send() do?
quiz.explanation: res.send() sends data back to the client.

chapters.title: Database Integration
chapters.description: Learn how to connect Node.js applications with databases like MySQL and MongoDB. Understand CRUD operations, ORM/ODM tools, and data modeling techniques.

pages.title: Connecting to MySQL
pages.content: Node.js can connect to MySQL databases using libraries like mysql2. This allows executing SQL queries from your application.

quiz.question: Which library is used to connect MySQL in Node.js?
quiz.explanation: mysql2 is used to connect MySQL in Node.js.

pages.title: Connecting to MongoDB
pages.content: MongoDB is a NoSQL database that stores data in JSON-like format. Node.js connects to MongoDB using libraries like mongoose.

quiz.question: Which library is used for MongoDB in Node.js?
quiz.explanation: mongoose is used to connect MongoDB.

pages.title: CRUD Operations
pages.content: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete. These operations allow managing data in databases.

quiz.question: What does CRUD stand for?
quiz.explanation: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, Delete.

pages.title: ORM/ODM (Mongoose, Sequelize)
pages.content: ORM (Object Relational Mapping) and ODM (Object Data Modeling) tools simplify database interactions by using objects instead of raw queries.

quiz.question: Which tool is used for MongoDB modeling?
quiz.explanation: Mongoose is used for MongoDB data modeling.

pages.title: Data Modeling
pages.content: Data modeling defines how data is structured in a database. It includes defining schemas, relationships, and constraints.

quiz.question: What is data modeling?
quiz.explanation: Data modeling defines how data is structured in a database.

chapters.title: Authentication & Security
chapters.description: Learn how to secure Node.js applications using authentication techniques like JWT, password hashing, authorization, middleware security, and environment variables.

pages.title: JWT Authentication
pages.content: JWT (JSON Web Token) is used to securely transmit information between client and server. It is commonly used for authentication in web applications.

quiz.question: What is JWT used for?
quiz.explanation: JWT is used for authentication.

pages.title: Password Hashing (bcrypt)
pages.content: Password hashing is used to store passwords securely. bcrypt is a popular library for hashing passwords in Node.js.

quiz.question: Why use password hashing?
quiz.explanation: Hashing protects passwords from being exposed.

pages.title: Authorization
pages.content: Authorization determines what a user is allowed to do after authentication. It ensures users access only permitted resources.

quiz.question: What is authorization?
quiz.explanation: Authorization controls access to resources.

pages.title: Middleware Security
pages.content: Middleware can be used to secure routes by checking authentication and permissions before allowing access.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of security middleware?
quiz.explanation: Security middleware protects routes from unauthorized access.

pages.title: Environment Variables
pages.content: Environment variables are used to store sensitive data like API keys and database credentials securely outside the code.

quiz.question: Why use environment variables?
quiz.explanation: Environment variables protect sensitive information.

chapters.title: File Upload & APIs
chapters.description: Learn how to handle file uploads, design APIs, manage JSON data, test APIs using tools, and implement proper error handling in Node.js applications.

pages.title: File Upload (Multer)
pages.content: Multer is a middleware used in Node.js for handling multipart/form-data, primarily used for uploading files.

quiz.question: Which library is used for file uploads?
quiz.explanation: Multer is used for handling file uploads.

pages.title: API Design Best Practices
pages.content: Good API design ensures clarity, scalability, and maintainability. It includes proper naming, versioning, and consistent response formats.

quiz.question: What is a good API practice?
quiz.explanation: Clear and consistent endpoints improve API design.

pages.title: Handling JSON Data
pages.content: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is commonly used to send and receive data in APIs. Node.js can easily parse and handle JSON.

quiz.question: What format is commonly used in APIs?
quiz.explanation: JSON is widely used for API communication.

pages.title: API Testing (Postman)
pages.content: Postman is a tool used to test APIs by sending requests and analyzing responses. It helps developers debug and validate APIs.

quiz.question: What is Postman used for?
quiz.explanation: Postman is used to test APIs.

pages.title: Error Handling
pages.content: Proper error handling ensures applications respond gracefully to failures. It includes handling server errors, validation errors, and unexpected issues.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of error handling?
quiz.explanation: Error handling ensures smooth application behavior during failures.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime environment that allows execution of JavaScript code on the server side.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the V8 engine?
interviewQuestions.answer: The V8 engine is Google's JavaScript engine used by Node.js to execute JavaScript code efficiently.

interviewQuestions.question: What is npm?
interviewQuestions.answer: npm (Node Package Manager) is used to install, manage, and share Node.js packages.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between Node.js and JavaScript?
interviewQuestions.answer: JavaScript is a programming language, while Node.js is a runtime environment that executes JavaScript outside the browser.

interviewQuestions.question: What is REPL in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: REPL stands for Read-Eval-Print Loop, which allows interactive execution of JavaScript code in the terminal.

interviewQuestions.question: What is asynchronous programming?
interviewQuestions.answer: Asynchronous programming allows tasks to run without blocking the execution of other operations.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a callback?
interviewQuestions.answer: A callback is a function passed as an argument to another function and executed after completion of a task.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a promise?
interviewQuestions.answer: A promise is an object representing the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation.

interviewQuestions.question: What is async/await?
interviewQuestions.answer: Async/await is a modern syntax for handling asynchronous operations in a more readable and synchronous-like manner.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the event loop?
interviewQuestions.answer: The event loop is a mechanism that handles asynchronous callbacks and ensures non-blocking execution in Node.js.

interviewQuestions.question: What are core modules in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Core modules are built-in modules like fs, http, path, and os that provide essential functionalities.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Express.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Express.js is a lightweight web framework for Node.js used to build web applications and APIs.

interviewQuestions.question: What is middleware in Express?
interviewQuestions.answer: Middleware functions execute during the request-response cycle and can modify requests or responses.

interviewQuestions.question: What is REST API?
interviewQuestions.answer: A REST API is an interface that allows communication between client and server using HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.

interviewQuestions.question: What is JWT?
interviewQuestions.answer: JWT (JSON Web Token) is used for secure authentication by transmitting information as a token.

interviewQuestions.question: What is bcrypt?
interviewQuestions.answer: bcrypt is a library used for hashing passwords securely in Node.js applications.

interviewQuestions.question: What is CRUD?
interviewQuestions.answer: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations used in database management.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code?
interviewQuestions.answer: Synchronous code executes line by line, while asynchronous code allows multiple operations to run concurrently without blocking.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a stream in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Streams are objects used to read or write data continuously instead of loading the entire data into memory.

interviewQuestions.question: What is clustering in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Clustering allows Node.js to create multiple processes to handle more load and improve performance.

interviewQuestions.question: What is child process in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Child processes allow Node.js to run other processes in parallel for heavy tasks.

interviewQuestions.question: What is rate limiting?
interviewQuestions.answer: Rate limiting restricts the number of requests a client can make to prevent abuse.

interviewQuestions.question: What is CORS?
interviewQuestions.answer: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is a security feature that controls access to resources from different origins.

interviewQuestions.question: What is process.env?
interviewQuestions.answer: process.env is used to access environment variables in Node.js.

interviewQuestions.question: What is load balancing?
interviewQuestions.answer: Load balancing distributes incoming requests across multiple servers to improve performance and reliability.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between require and import?
interviewQuestions.answer: require is used in CommonJS modules, while import is used in ES modules for loading dependencies.

interviewQuestions.question: What is event emitter?
interviewQuestions.answer: EventEmitter is a class used to handle custom events in Node.js.

interviewQuestions.question: How do you handle errors in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: Errors can be handled using try/catch, callbacks, promises (.catch), and middleware in Express.
